gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Sun Gold Power's 6000W 48V split-phase inverter/charger 'requires 240VAC input'. Feeding it from a 120 V-only source, such as the 120 V outlet on most portable generators, does not meet that requirement, so plan on a 240 V generator or 240 V feed to recharge the battery bank through it.
standout_why: ChatGPT's results list was empty in both saved chats (2026-11-14T04:39 and 04:47), so there are no rival pages to compare. Its own answer covers backfeed and transfer equipment, permits, a licensed electrician, 'mutually compatible equipment' and avoiding bare cells. It names EG4, Sol-Ark and Victron inverters, but it never mentions the AC-input voltage the inverter/charger needs in order to charge, or that a 120 V generator may not meet it. The finding is new and changes which generator or inverter belongs in the set. It is not scored 3 because the forum thread showing what happens in practice could not be opened (it returned 403).
kit_items: inverter/charger: Sun Gold Power 6000W 48V Split Phase Pure Sine Wave Inverter with Charger (UL1741). It has a built-in AC auto-transfer switch and Auto Gen Start. Its listing says it requires 240 VAC input, so pair it with a 240 V source.

battery: Sun Gold Power SG48100P 51.2V 100Ah server-rack LiFePO4 (UL1973, UL9540A, CAN/RS485/RS232). It is sold by the same store as the inverter, so one cart covers the set. The store's 2-pack (about 10.24 kWh) suits multi-hour backup.

alternative inverter if the shopper only has 120 V charging power: Sun Gold Power SPH5048P 5000W 48V. Its listing gives a 40–60 V battery charging range and an RS485 port for BMS communication, and states a 120 V single-phase output. Its required AC input voltage was not confirmed.

The 6000W LF manual (LFP6K48V240VSP PDF on solartown.com) for the exact AC-input wiring, behaviour on 120 V-only input, neutral-ground bonding, lithium DIP-switch charge voltages and DC fuse sizing. The site returned HTTP 403, and downloading it locally was not permitted.
